hypothesis: RETROSPECTIVE CORRECTION of the original 240-cell sweep, not a new test: does any cell beat cash once the search itself is accounted for?
test: Hansen (2005) SPA with the Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap and Politis-White automatic block length; White (2000) Reality Check; Romano-Wolf (2005) stepdown; Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014) deflated Sharpe
data: 228 usable cells of the original sweep, refit and aligned on a common 2h clock
config: benchmark = cash (the generous bar); B bootstrap index vectors shared across cells so cross-sectional dependence is resampled rather than assumed away
statistic: SPA consistent p 0.340 (bracket 0.299-0.340), Reality Check 0.483, Romano-Wolf rejects nothing, deflated Sharpe 0.400. Winner NEAR/30m/hmm: t=2.47, naive one-sided p 0.0067, Sharpe 0.134 against an expected no-skill maximum of 0.150.
verdict: The 0.035 in the README is the minimum of 228 dependent draws; under a pure null the expected minimum is about 1/229 = 0.004, so 0.035 is LESS extreme than chance predicts. Correctly computed, the sweep's p-value is 0.34. Bonferroni, Holm and BHY all leave zero survivors, and the largest t-statistic anywhere in the sweep is 2.47 against the Harvey-Liu-Zhu hurdle of 3.0.
note: Logged with id 0 because it is the correction of work that preceded this registry, not a member of its family.

hypothesis: A fixed 3-state HSMM, applied identically to every top-30 perp at 30m, carries timing information across the market.
test: pooled panel permutation, common circular rotation of the whole position matrix (preserves cross-sectional dependence and per-coin turnover)
config: hsmm, states=3, maxDuration=30, duration-aware entry, walk-forward train 1080/test 360, seed 42
verdict: Not merely non-significant: the model's own positions, rotated to random times, beat the times it actually chose in 98.4% of 5000 draws. Whatever the regime filter is keying on, it enters late enough that the alignment costs money. One test, no selection, so no correction applies.
statistic: pooled mean net return 1.521 bps/bar vs null median 2.217

hypothesis: Setting aside tradeability, the same fixed HSMM's expected next-bar return correlates with the realized next-bar return across the market.
test: pooled information coefficient (Mincer-Zarnowitz slope + Pearson IC), common circular rotation null
data: top 30 Hyperliquid perps, 30m, 45 days to 2026-09-11 (28 with enough history)
config: identical to test 1 — same fit, same walk-forward, forecasts read before quantization
verdict: No forecasting content at the one-bar horizon. Note the sign split: Pearson IC positive, Spearman negative. A positive linear correlation with a negative rank correlation means the whole of the apparent relationship sits in a handful of large-magnitude bars while the typical bar runs the other way — the signature of a Gaussian-emission model spending its states on kurtosis instead of regimes.
note: Uses every out-of-sample bar rather than only the traded ones, so it has far more power than test 1. Registered before the result was known.
statistic: pooled IC 0.01081 (rank IC -0.01670, MZ slope 0.190) vs null median 0.00347, 90% band [-0.01342, 0.02222]

hypothesis: The model's forecast predicts the return over the horizon it actually claims — its own learned dwell (~9 bars at 30m) — rather than the single next bar.
test: pooled IC of the expected next-bar return against the forward cumulative return over h bars, common circular rotation null (which preserves the autocorrelation that overlapping windows induce)
data: same 29-coin panel, no refit, no new data
config: h fixed at 9 in advance, taken from the median learned dwell the fit already reported; other horizons recorded as exploratory
verdict: Not significant at the horizon the model itself claims. Exploratory horizons h=1,2,4,18,48 all non-significant too (best p=0.35 at h=18); recorded here so the family count includes them rather than pretending only the pre-registered one was looked at.
note: Not a fishing expedition for a better horizon: a model that says regimes last nine bars is making a nine-bar claim, and testing it one bar out tests something it never asserted.

hypothesis: POST HOC, and flagged as such: the model's rank correlation with future returns is non-zero — it came out negative at all six horizons tried, which is what prompted the test.
test: two-sided permutation on the pooled Spearman IC, common rotation null
data: same 29-coin panel — the same data the pattern was spotted in, which is precisely why this cannot confirm anything
config: two-sided deliberately: a one-sided test chosen after seeing the sign is a description, not a test
verdict: Does not survive the family correction at n=4 except marginally at h=2, and it was found in the data it was tested on. Registered as a hypothesis to confirm, not as a result.
note: With four registered tests the Bonferroni bar is 0.0125. Even if this clears it, the only thing that would make it real is confirmation on a window this test never touched.

hypothesis: CONFIRMATION, direction fixed in advance by test 4: on a window never previously examined, the mean rank IC of the same model's forecast across horizons h=1,2,4 is NEGATIVE.
test: one-sided lower-tail permutation on the composite mean rank IC, common circular rotation null, 5000 draws. One-sided is legitimate here and only here: the sign comes from a different window's data, not from this one's.
data: top 30 Hyperliquid perps, 30m, the OLDEST 2840 of 5000 retained candles (~59 days ending where the 45-day window used by tests 1-4 begins). Strictly disjoint from every previous test.
config: identical model, identical walk-forward, identical features. Nothing tuned. Composite over h=1,2,4 chosen to avoid selecting the horizon that looked best in test 4.
verdict: NOT CONFIRMED. The statistic sits essentially on the null, and at h=1 it flipped sign outright. Test 4 was noise, as the family count said it probably was. The candidate is dead and the registry says so permanently.
note: This is the only test in the file that could turn test 4's observation into a finding. It runs once. If it fails, test 4 was the 1-in-20 and that is the answer.
statistic: composite mean rank IC -0.00113 on 39,862 held-out observations, against a null median of +0.00497 and a 90% band of [-0.0114, 0.0335]. Two-sided 0.5965. Per horizon: h=1 +0.00046, h=2 -0.00151, h=4 -0.00234, h=9 -0.00496. P&L on the same window -0.172 bps/bar, p=0.6491.

hypothesis: The same fixed HSMM carries timing information, tested where the study is actually powered: 4h bars over the full ~833 days Hyperliquid retains, rather than 45 days at 30m.
test: pooled panel permutation, common circular rotation null, 5000 draws; plus the pooled forecast IC at h=1 and at the learned dwell
data: top 30 Hyperliquid perps, 4h, up to 5000 bars each (~2.3 years). Coins listed too recently are dropped rather than padded.
config: identical model, identical walk-forward, identical features. The ONLY thing changed from test 1 is the calendar span, which is the binding constraint the power analysis identified.
verdict: Not significant, and this time that means something. At 582 days the test had ~100% power to detect the 3.11 annual Sharpe the model's own posterior implies, so this is a null result with teeth rather than an underpowered shrug: an edge of the claimed size would have shown up and did not. What survives is an edge no larger than about 1.5 bps/bar in 30m terms (annual Sharpe ~1.33), against a 0.9 bps/bar break-even. Resolving THAT would take 2.6 years of history; Hyperliquid retains 1.6.
note: Power, not fishing. src/power.ts: 45 days at 30m resolves an annual Sharpe of 7.08 at 80% power, while the model's own posterior implies 3.11 — the earlier tests had 19% power at alpha=0.05 and 0% at the sweep's corrected alpha, so their large p-values carried almost no information. 833 days resolves 1.65. This is the first test in the file capable of detecting the effect it is looking for.
statistic: 27 coins, 74,603 observations, 582-day median span. Pooled net 0.262 bps/bar against a null median of -0.151, 90% band [-0.882, 0.564]. Forecast IC 0.00287 at h=1 (p 0.40) and 0.01064 at h=9 (p 0.32); rank IC positive at both, which retires test 4's negative sign for good.
